field_conventions.cbm_edge: UPPERCASE_SNAKE_CASE identifier from CBM analyzer output (e.g., 'HTTP_CALLS', 'HANDLES')
field_conventions.dr_relationship: predicate name from predicates.json or null if unmappable
field_conventions.usage: edge classification: 'verification_and_mapping' for edges that create DR relationships, 'traversal_only' for edges used as evidence, provenance or traversal input; implementation_note says why an edge is traversal-only, and names the catalog addition it waits on when that is the reason
field_conventions.dr_scope: scope of the relationship (intra-layer, cross-layer, both)
field_conventions.direction: relationship direction (forward, backward, bidirectional, or caller_to_callee)
field_conventions.confidence_from_property: code property that determines confidence level (e.g., visibility, export status)
field_conventions.dr_pattern: '<source layer.type> → <destination layer.type>' of the DR relationship, after directionality_transform; for verification_and_mapping edges it must name a triple in the relationship catalog
field_conventions.order: the first mapping is the call-graph default edge type, so CALLS comes first
field_conventions.conditions: for verification_and_mapping edges: predicates lists, in order of preference, the predicates that can express the edge ({predicate, invert}; invert when the DR relationship runs from the CBM edge's target to its source). from_types and to_types, when present, restrict the element types the CBM edge's source and target may have ('layer.type' or 'layer.*'); an edge between other types creates no relationship. A preference may carry its own from_types and to_types; one that names both is a scoped pair, which the mapping-level from_types and to_types do not restrict (USAGE from a technology node to its image). The relationship is the first catalog triple that exists between the two classified element types (cli/src/analyzers/edge-relationships.ts); dr_relationship, directionality_transform and dr_pattern describe one listed preference and a typical case. 'gate' is a note on what the caller must ensure

mappings.description: A function calls another function: the caller depends on the callee
mappings.implementation_note: Listed first: it is the call-graph default edge type for dr analyzer callers and callees. Creates a relationship only between functions that both survive classification. A call from a test case to the code it exercises (a component, function, process, interface, service, operation, object schema or access pattern) is the test testing it (testing.testcasesketch.tests.*); a call to a member with no element of its own counts as a call to its class, and from a test only when the test's file refers to that class (a USAGE or IMPORTS edge), because the index resolves a call by the member's name.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own. The edge itself passes the call-edge evidence gate (heuristic call_edge_evidence): below confidence 0.5 a name-only resolution needs corroboration

mappings.description: A function or method handles an HTTP route: the API operation for that route realizes the application function
mappings.implementation_note: CBM writes the edge handler → Route; the DR relationship runs from the operation to the function it realizes (api.operation.realizes.application.applicationfunction), so the direction is inverted. HANDLES names routes by path while Route nodes are named __route__METHOD__/path.

mappings.description: A class defines a method: the application component is assigned the application function
mappings.implementation_note: Deterministic. A controller class (application interface) defining its route handlers (application functions) creates no relationship here: the catalog has no interface-to-function structural triple, and the operation side comes from HANDLES.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: Module or file import dependency: one application component uses another
mappings.implementation_note: Only between application-layer elements (component to component, or a component or function to the data object a module defines); imports of external packages, and of anything else, stay traversal input (datastore detection reads them).

mappings.description: A callable is used as a value (handler or callback registration): the registering function depends on it
mappings.implementation_note: Same treatment as CALLS.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: A request crosses a route: data flows from the code that calls an HTTP or async route to the function that handles it
mappings.implementation_note: Not a local argument-to-parameter edge. CBM's route pass writes it only from the source of an HTTP_CALLS or ASYNC_CALLS edge into a Route to that Route's handler (its HANDLES source, or a handler reached through INFRA_MAPS), and skips it when the caller already CALLS the handler (src/pipeline/pass_route_nodes.c:746, CBM 0.12.1). Properties: via (the route's name), route (its qualified name), edge_type (HTTP_CALLS or ASYNC_CALLS), via_infra, handler_params and caller_args (the argument-to-parameter mapping). Not observed in the eval corpora, which have no in-repository client of their own routes. The fallback to depends-on is dropped: a caller depends on the operation, not on the code behind it.

conditions.gate: both ends kept by Tier-1 significance gating; most functions are not elements on their own

mappings.description: A function or component uses a data structure without calling it: it accesses the data object
mappings.implementation_note: The largest-reach edge (387 gold cards). Map only when the target was accepted as a data object (an Interface, Type, Enum or data class); usage of variables and anything else is traversal only. CBM rates USAGE as identifier use without a proven target, so confidence is low. A function or component using a data-model object schema (an entity class) accesses it, as it accesses a data object. CBM also records a workload or compose service referring to its container image (ref: image) as USAGE: a technology.node to a technology.artifact is the node composing the image it runs (technology.node.composes.technology.artifact), a scoped-pair preference outside the data-object to_types.

mappings.description: A function or component mutates a data structure's state: it accesses the data object
mappings.implementation_note: Same targets as USAGE; writing is access, so the provider reading (serves) does not apply.

mappings.description: A class implements an interface that was classified as an application interface: the component provides that interface
mappings.implementation_note: Only when the implemented interface was accepted as application.applicationinterface. Implementing a data-object interface creates no relationship (the catalog has no component-to-dataobject structural triple, by design).

mappings.description: A test function exercises a symbol: the test case sketch tests that component, function, interface, service, operation, object schema or access pattern
mappings.implementation_note: From a test case (a test function Tier 0 classified as testing.testcasesketch) to the production symbol it exercises, when that symbol is an accepted element; calls into builtins, helpers and unclassified symbols create nothing.

mappings.description: A test file covers a source file: the coverage target covers the component
mappings.implementation_note: File-level counterpart of TESTS; same test pass.

mappings.description: A function publishes to a queue or topic: it raises the application event the queue carries
mappings.implementation_note: Inert (2026-11-12, #1080): the target is an async Route (__route__<transport>__..., e.g. __route__kafka__orders), and no node mapping or Tier-0 rule makes one an element: extraction reads only HTTP-method routes (parseRouteName), and the queue's Channel is unmapped. The mapping it stood for, application.applicationfunction.triggers.application.applicationevent (in the catalog since 2026-11-05), comes back once a rule classifies async Routes and Channels as application events.

mappings.description: A function listens on a channel: the application event triggers the handler function
mappings.implementation_note: Inert (2026-11-12, same cause as ASYNC_CALLS, #1080): CBM writes listener → Channel or async Route, and neither becomes an element. Once a rule classifies them as application events, map it inverted: application.applicationevent.triggers.application.applicationfunction. The interface-level reading waits on catalog addition 4.

mappings.description: Code starts an external program: the system software serves the calling component
mappings.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes caller → Process, the catalog has technology.systemsoftware.serves.application.applicationcomponent. Observed on CBM 0.12.1 (61 / 3 / 2 on dr-cli / fastapi / petclinic: git, node, bun, gh, claude and other programs the code or its scripts launch). Process maps to technology.systemsoftware since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9), so the edge creates a relationship when its caller is an application component; the catalog has no triple from an application function, a script or a Dockerfile (a Module with no card) to system software, so most observed SPAWNS still create none.

mappings.description: Infrastructure dependency between artifacts (charts, packages, base images) or system software
mappings.implementation_note: Infrastructure only: Helm chart dependencies, go.mod / requirements.txt to a Package, a Dockerfile to its base Images and an Image to its Dockerfile, compose depends_on and links (CBM 0.12.1; observed 0 / 12 / 1). Creates a relationship only between infrastructure elements (mapped since 2026-11-12, inventory step 9): compose depends_on between services is technology.node depends-on technology.node, an image on an image technology.artifact depends-on technology.artifact. A Dockerfile is a Module with no card, so the Dockerfile-to-image and image-to-Dockerfile edges create none, and an image is not linked to its base images through its Dockerfile.

mappings.description: A Kubernetes Service selects workloads: each workload node realizes the technology service
mappings.implementation_note: Inverted: CBM writes Service → workload. Observed on CBM 0.12.1 (petclinic 2: k8s Service to Deployment). Resource maps by kind since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9: Deployment to technology.node, Service to technology.technologyservice), so each edge creates technology.node realizes technology.technologyservice.

mappings.description: What deploys (a CI job, a script or Make rule, a Flux or Argo object, a Helm chart, a Terraform release) to what it deploys (manifests, Kubernetes objects, charts, images): the deploying artifact aggregates what it puts on a cluster
mappings.implementation_note: Not inverted: CBM writes deployer → deployed, and has no cluster node (README 0.12.1 'DEPLOYS'; src/pipeline/pass_k8s.c, pass_shell.c, pass_terraform.c, pass_operator.c, pass_ansible.c). Observed on CBM 0.12.1: petclinic's Module .github/workflows/deploy-and-test-cluster.yml DEPLOYS File k8s/db.yml. The deployer is a Module or Function (a workflow, script, Make rule, Go installer), a Resource (Flux or Argo object, Terraform resource) or a Chart; the deployed end is a File, Resource, Chart or Image. Resource, Chart and Image map to technology types since 2026-11-12 (inventory step 9), so a Chart, Flux, Argo or Terraform deployer that is an element links to what it deploys; a CI workflow or script deployer is a Module or Function with no technology element, and a deployed manifest is a File, so petclinic's two edges still create none. from_types keeps a CI module or script function, which the node mapping places in the application layer, from linking to an artifact.

mappings.description: Outbound HTTP call to an API route. From a test case it is the test exercising that operation
mappings.implementation_note: Creates a relationship only from a test case (a symbol Tier 0 classified as testing.testcasesketch) to an operation: on CBM 0.12.1 almost every observed caller is test code (53 of 55 on fastapi, 81 of 86 on dr-cli). A production caller (application code consuming an operation) still creates none: that triple waits on catalog addition 7 (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md), queued in Context Studio. Extraction also reads this edge from test code that calls a served route by URL (MockMvc get("/owners/{ownerId}"), RestTemplate, supertest), which CBM has no edge for.

mappings.description: Outbound gRPC call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Outbound GraphQL call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS. Emitted by CBM 0.12.1 (src/pipeline/pass_parallel.c, from a GraphQL client call to the operation's Route) but missing from its README edge list: emitted and undocumented, not binary-only. Proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Outbound tRPC call
mappings.implementation_note: Same as HTTP_CALLS. Emitted by CBM 0.12.1 (src/pipeline/pass_parallel.c, from a tRPC client call to the procedure's Route) but missing from its README edge list: emitted and undocumented, not binary-only. Proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 7); map once accepted.

mappings.description: Class or interface inheritance: the subclass specializes its parent
mappings.implementation_note: Only between two elements of the same type that the catalog lets specialize (object schemas, data objects, components, functions, ...): an entity class extending a mapped superclass. Inheriting from a class of another type, or from one that is not an element, creates nothing.

mappings.description: Class or interface extension
mappings.implementation_note: In the CBM binary only (0.10.2 and 0.12.1), not in its documented vocabulary or any observed graph; kept for forward compatibility. INHERITS is the edge CBM emits for class extension.

mappings.description: Method override
mappings.implementation_note: specializes between functions; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 2); map once accepted. Also Kustomize patches in infrastructure.

mappings.description: A function emits on a channel
mappings.implementation_note: triggers an application event from a function or component; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A function raises an exception class
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for error-handling concerns; triggers an application event when the exception is a domain event, proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 3); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A method throws an exception class
mappings.implementation_note: Same as RAISES: evidence for error-handling concerns; the triggers reading waits on catalog addition 3.

mappings.description: Folder contains folder
mappings.implementation_note: composes between directory-level components; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 5); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A workload addresses a Service
mappings.implementation_note: depends-on from a node to a technology service; proposed to Context Studio's review queue as a catalog addition (docs/analyzers/CBM_MAPPING_INVENTORY.md, addition 9); map once accepted.

mappings.description: A file defines a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Provenance: supplies source_reference.file for every element mapped from a symbol. Not a relationship between elements.

mappings.description: A decorator applies to a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence: decorator names feed the Tier-0 rules (extraction-heuristics.json) and the card. Decorator is not an element.

mappings.description: A symbol reads a config key, or a config key names a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for security and APM concerns (EnvVar is not an element).

mappings.description: Folder contains file
mappings.implementation_note: Traversal only: the directory structure behind placement facts.

mappings.description: Vocabulary-mismatch similarity (score >= 0.80)
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for Tier-0 clustering and duplicate detection.

mappings.description: MinHash near-clone
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; for duplicate detection.

mappings.description: Files that change together in history
mappings.implementation_note: No DR counterpart; evidence for component boundaries.

mappings.description: Git branch metadata
mappings.implementation_note: Provenance for source_reference; not a relationship.

mappings.description: Documentation references a file
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

mappings.description: Documentation mentions a symbol
mappings.implementation_note: Evidence for descriptions and for Tier 2's upper-layer inference.

mappings.description: A function reads a field or variable
mappings.implementation_note: The read half of WRITES: CBM 0.12.1 writes READS or WRITES for each member access (src/pipeline/pass_usages.c, pass_parallel.c), but its README edge list omits READS. Traversal input only for now: USAGE already links a reader to the type it reads, and the field or variable end is below element granularity.

mappings.description: An architecture decision record supersedes an earlier one
mappings.implementation_note: New in CBM 0.12.0: links ADR nodes, from the newer record to the one it supersedes. ADR has no node mapping (a decision record states intent, which the rules never decide). codebase_extract reads the edge to retire the older record: it gets no decision-record card, and an element sourced only from it is a candidate delete.

mappings.description: An arrow between two elements of a diagram (Mermaid, PlantUML, Graphviz, D2, draw.io, Excalidraw)
mappings.implementation_note: New in CBM 0.12.0 (src/pipeline/pass_diagrams.c): links DiagramElement nodes. A diagram states what someone drew, not what the code does: evidence for Tier 2's upper-layer inference at most.

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Federated extraction (2026-11-12, opt-in with codebase_index crossRepo; cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts). CBM 0.12.1 writes it from the caller to its own client Route, with target_project, target_function, target_file, url_path and (when the caller names the method) transport; the serving project gets a copy from the handler pointing back at one caller, which is skipped. It becomes a qualified cross-model reference on the caller's element (references field, @model/layer.type.name), not a relationship, so usage stays traversal_only. Predicate: the first catalog triple from the caller's type to the other model's api.operation (tests, triggers, references), else to the handler's element (flows-to, from application code, as DATA_FLOWS). An application caller has no triple to api.operation (catalog addition 7).

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (the fixture repositories produced only CROSS_HTTP_CALLS and CROSS_CHANNEL), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Not mapped: not observed on CBM 0.12.1 (a Kafka producer and consumer in two fixture repositories linked as CROSS_CHANNEL, not this), so its shape is unknown. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out (cli/src/analyzers/cross-model.ts).

mappings.description: Cross-repository call or channel
mappings.implementation_note: Not mapped. CBM 0.12.1 writes it from the emitting or listening file (EMITS and LISTENS_ON have file sources) to its own Channel, with target_project, target_function (the other file's name), target_file, channel_name and transport, in both projects; the edge does not say which side emits. Neither side's Channel is an element (no rule makes one an application event yet, #1080), so there is no target for a reference. Federated extraction counts it and leaves it out.
